story: Alaska's Division of Elections told legislators that more than 600 of the roughly 3,000 people it moved off the active voter list after a DMV records comparison were in fact U.S. citizens, and it has paused further comparisons eleven days before the August 18th primary

claims.claim: More than 600 U.S. citizens were mistakenly flagged as possible noncitizens and removed from Alaska's list of active voters, according to the Division of Elections director's letter to lawmakers.
claims.claim_verbatim: More than 600 U.S. citizens were mistakenly flagged as possible noncitizens and removed from Alaska's list of active voters earlier this year, the director of the Alaska Division of Elections said Thursday in a letter responding to questions from state lawmakers.
claims.notes: Read in the Alaska Beacon RSS feed, which carries full article text where the article page 403s. The Beecher letter is posted on elections.alaska.gov ONLY AS IMAGES, so this figure is the newsroom's reading of a primary document the run could not read. 600 is a floor, not a total, and is NOT the count who contacted the division (see C04).

claims.claim: The Beacon reported that 3,058 people were removed from Alaska's active voter list after the Division of Elections compared its citizenship data against Division of Motor Vehicles records.
claims.claim_verbatim: Those citizens were among 3,058 people removed from the list after the division compared its citizenship data to a separate set of records kept by the Alaska Division of Motor Vehicles.
claims.notes: Use the word inactive or off the active list alongside any use of removed, because the Division's framing and the earlier reporting both say inactive and these people may still cast a ballot (C12).
claims.conflict: CONFLICTS WITH C03. Alaska Public Media reported 3,048 on 2026-07-23 from a division spokesman; the Beacon reports 3,058 on 2026-08-06. Difference of 10. NO FETCHED PAGE RECONCILES THEM. The deck says roughly 3,000 or gives both with outlet and date.

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported on July 23rd, 2026 that a Division of Elections spokesman gave the specific figure of 3,048.
claims.claim_verbatim: A spokesman for the division later provided a specific number: 3,048
claims.notes: Re-fetched and reconfirmed 2026-08-07. This is the figure the August 1st deck used. The verbatim contains a colon, so it may not be set on a slide as printed.

claims.claim: Elections Director Carol Beecher wrote that approximately 685 voters have contacted the Division and stated they are citizens despite the inconsistency with the DMV's records.
claims.claim_verbatim: Approximately 685 voters have contacted the Division and stated they are citizens, despite the inconsistency with the DMV's records,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting the Beecher letter
claims.notes: 685 ASSERTED citizenship; more than 600 is the number the division accepted as citizens. Different quantities, never interchangeable. Beecher's own hedge Approximately must not be hardened.

claims.claim: Beecher wrote that more than 100 people have reported they are not citizens and requested that their voter registration be cancelled.
claims.claim_verbatim: more than 100 people have reported they are not citizens and requested that their voter registration be cancelled
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting the Beecher letter
claims.notes: REQUIRED FOR FAIRNESS. This is the part of the comparison that found something. The deck carries it if it carries the 600. No fetched page says any of these people voted or attempted to vote.

claims.claim: About 350 of the letters the Division of Elections sent to affected Alaskans were returned as undeliverable.
claims.claim_verbatim: About 350 letters were returned as undeliverable
claims.notes: Reporter's summary rather than a quoted line from the letter. The hedge About is the outlet's and must be kept.

claims.claim: About 1,900 affected Alaskans have not responded at all to the Division's letter.
claims.claim_verbatim: another 1,900 affected Alaskans have not responded at all
claims.notes: The number is solid. The source's following clause about them being unaware is the reporter's INFERENCE and must be attributed or dropped. Arithmetic check, 685 plus 100 plus 350 plus 1,900 is about 3,035, short of both 3,048 and 3,058, so these four are NOT an exhaustive breakdown.

claims.claim: In 2024 the DMV and the Division of Elections compared just 2,000 records.
claims.claim_verbatim: In 2024, for example, DMV and DOE compared just 2,000 records
claims.notes: The scale contrast, with C09 the strongest number pair in the story. The full source sentence contains an em dash, so this excerpt is cut before it.

claims.claim: More than 580,000 records were compared this year, a volume the DMV called non-routine.
claims.claim_verbatim: not the more than 580,000 compared this year, which DMV called "non-routine."
claims.notes: The word non-routine is attributed by the Beacon to the DMV. The primary joint statement publishes as an IMAGE ONLY, so the word could not be read at source. Attribute on slide as per the Alaska Beacon.

claims.claim: Beecher wrote that the Division has paused additional DMV comparisons while it evaluates this initial effort and incorporates lessons learned.
claims.claim_verbatim: the Division has paused additional DMV comparisons while it evaluates this initial effort and incorporates lessons learned.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting the Beecher letter
claims.notes: THE NEWS PEG. Paused, not stopped and not reversed. The deck must not say the program was cancelled.

claims.claim: Beecher said she will not unilaterally return affected Alaskans to the voter rolls and that the division will instead send out another notice to affected voters.
claims.claim_verbatim: Beecher said she will not unilaterally return affected Alaskans to the voter rolls. The division will instead send out another notice to affected voters, she said.
claims.notes: RESOLVES THE AUGUST 1st DECK'S OPEN QUESTION. As of 2026-08-06 there is no blanket restoration, a second notice instead. No date is given for that notice and the primary is August 18th. The deck must not assert it will or will not arrive in time.

claims.claim: Someone removed from the voter list may still cast a vote this year but will not appear on their precinct register and must provide additional identity information to cast a questioned ballot.
claims.claim_verbatim: Someone removed from the voter list may still cast a vote this year, but they will not appear on the register of their local precinct and will have to provide additional identity information in order to cast a "questioned ballot."
claims.notes: THE ACTIONABLE CORE, and the best-supported fact in the run. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media 2026-07-23 and by the joint agency statement quoted by Alaska's News Source. COUNTERWEIGHT, the deck says a questioned ballot CAN BE CAST and must not say it WILL BE COUNTED (see C24).

claims.claim: A joint statement from the Division of Motor Vehicles and the Division of Elections said Elections most recently asked DMV to compare lists in March 2026, producing the letters that were recently sent.
claims.claim_verbatim: Elections most recently asked DMV to compare lists in March 2026, resulting in the 3,000 letters that Elections recently sent.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska's News Source, quoting the joint DMV and Division of Elections statement
claims.notes: THE MECHANISM IN THE AGENCIES' OWN WORDS. One agency asked another to compare two lists. NOT AN AI SYSTEM. No fetched page in this run uses artificial intelligence, algorithm, machine learning or model anywhere in this story. The primary version is posted as an IMAGE.

claims.claim: Beecher said the Division of Elections sent a letter to about 3,500 Alaskans.
claims.claim_verbatim: She said her agency sent a letter to about 3,500 Alaskans.
claims.notes: LETTERS MAILED IS A DIFFERENT QUANTITY FROM REGISTRATIONS MOVED. Do not conflate with C02 or C03. Best practice is to build no slide on the letter count at all.
claims.conflict: About 3,500 per Alaska Public Media versus 3,000 in the joint agency statement. Unreconciled.

claims.claim: A bipartisan group of 23 legislators wrote to Elections Director Carol Beecher asking that all names be put back on the active voters list unless ineligibility has been established.
claims.claim_verbatim: A bipartisan group of 23 legislators wrote a letter Tuesday, asking Elections Director Carol Beecher to put all names back on the active voters list unless their ineligibility to vote has been established.
claims.notes: This is the request the August 6th letter answers, so it is the hinge between the two decks. Present it as a REQUEST. The deck must NOT assert the removals were illegal; that word is the legislators' allegation and is not adjudicated.
claims.conflict: Alaska's News Source described the same letter as signed by 20 members of the bipartisan majority. Attribute or give the range; do not print a bare number.

claims.claim: KMXT reported that Beecher told legislators voters could get back on the voter list by contacting the division and affirming that they are citizens.
claims.claim_verbatim: voters could get back on the voter list by contacting the division and affirming that they are citizens
claims.notes: THE SECOND HALF OF THE ACTIONABLE CORE, and why a registration deadline is not the operative constraint. Affected voters REACTIVATE an existing registration rather than filing a new one. Corroborated by Alaska Public Media 2026-07-23. NO FETCHED PAGE STATES A DEADLINE for doing this, so the deck must not invent one.

claims.claim: The Alaska Division of Elections posted a notice titled Division of Elections responds to lawmakers' inquiry on August 6th, 2026.
claims.claim_verbatim: Division of Elections responds to lawmakers' inquiry
claims.notes: PRIMARY, and the only thing on that page that could honestly be verified. THE BEECHER LETTER IS PUBLISHED AS THREE EMBEDDED IMAGES WITH NO ALT TEXT AND NO TEXT LAYER. Every number attributed to that letter reaches the deck through the Alaska Beacon's reading of it, and the deck should say so once.

claims.claim: The Alaska Division of Elections lists the 2026 primary election as August 18, 2026 and the general election as November 3, 2026.
claims.claim_verbatim: August 18, 2026
claims.notes: PRIMARY, fetched 2026-08-07. Eleven days after this run date.

claims.claim: The Division of Elections says absentee in person and early voting locations are open for voting starting 15 days prior to and through Election Day.
claims.claim_verbatim: Absentee In-Person and Early Voting locations are open for voting starting 15 days prior and through Election Day.
claims.notes: PRIMARY. THE RULE IS VERBATIM, THE CALENDAR DATE IS DERIVED. 15 days before August 18th is August 3rd, so early voting is already open, but the page prints the rule and not that date.

claims.claim: The deadline to request an absentee ballot by mail for the 2026 primary is August 8th, 2026.
claims.claim_verbatim: August 8, 2026: Deadline to request an absentee ballot by mail
claims.notes: PRIMARY, and independently listed on the Division's home page. THE MOST TIME URGENT ITEM IN THE DECK, one day after this run date. Ballot return is postmarked or received by August 18th, 2026. The verbatim as listed carries a colon and must be restated on a slide, not quoted.

claims.claim: Public Citizen's election deepfake legislation tracker lists Alaska Senate Bill 64 with its election deepfake provision removed, and does not list Alaska among enacted states.
claims.claim_verbatim: Alaska | SB 64 | Introduced Jan. 2025, Passed Senate May 2025, Passed House 2026, Election deepfake provision removed
claims.notes: NEEDS ATTRIBUTION ON EVERY USE. An advocacy organisation's tracker, not a legislative record. akleg.gov, legiscan.com and congress.gov all 403, so the bill text could not be read. NO STATE COUNT SURVIVES from this page; its prose said 17 while its table listed 27.
claims.conflict: The tracker's stated enacted-state count and its own enacted rows disagree. No state count may be printed.

claims.claim: The Alaska Legislature passed a bipartisan elections bill, Senate Bill 64, that would have improved voter roll list maintenance, and Gov. Mike Dunleavy vetoed it before an override attempt failed.
claims.claim_verbatim: The Alaska Legislature attempted but failed to override Dunleavy's veto, with two Republican lawmakers, both from Southeast Alaska, providing the key votes to uphold the governor's decision.
claims.notes: NEEDS SOFTENING. That SB 64 would have improved list maintenance is Rep. Ashley Carrick's characterisation and must be attributed to her. NO FETCHED PAGE GIVES A VETO DATE, so the deck must not date it. The governor's newsroom carried no veto message and akleg.gov 403s.

claims.claim: The Division of Elections disclosed a list last year which showed 70 noncitizens either voted or attempted to vote in elections over the past decade.
claims.claim_verbatim: The division disclosed a similar list last year, which showed 70 noncitizens either voted or attempted to vote in elections over the past decade.
claims.notes: BACKGROUND, and the best available denominator. The deck may set 70 over a decade beside more than 580,000 records compared in one pass but must assert NO causal or policy conclusion, and must not imply the 70 are the same population as the 3,058. The compound either voted or attempted to vote must be kept whole.

claims.claim: Beecher dismissed an Anchorage temporary poll worker after she raised concerns about how poll workers were instructed to handle voters flagged as possible noncitizens.
claims.claim_verbatim: We are not confident that you will follow these instructions and for that reason we will no longer require your services as a Poll Worker for the August 18 Primary Election or the November 3, General Election,
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Beacon (James Brooks), quoting an email from Carol Beecher
claims.notes: SINGLE SOURCED and the Division has not responded to the Beacon, so any use must say so. The poll worker's concern that such ballots will not be counted is HER CHARACTERISATION and NO fetched page establishes it. THE DECK MUST NOT CLAIM THE BALLOTS WILL NOT BE COUNTED. Optional material.
